what: Carlyle is one of the original private equity firms. It buys companies, lends to them, invests in infrastructure and property, and manages insurance assets, charging fees on the money it is given and a share of the profits.
customers: Pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers and wealthy individuals committing capital for long periods.
money: direct lending, structured credit and insurance assets
funds that invest in other funds and secondaries
moat: A four-decade record and relationships with the institutions that allocate capital, which is what lets a firm raise a multi-billion-dollar fund at all.
risks: Performance fees depend on selling portfolio companies, and exits have been slow
Revenue swung from $8.8B to $3.0B and back to $4.8B in four years: the earnings are lumpy
40 times earnings on a profit figure that moves with markets
opportunities: Analysts see about 31% upside, with 19 covering the stock
$2.0B of cash against $470M of debt at the management company level
The credit and insurance businesses earn steady fees that do not depend on exits
watch: Fee-earning assets under management and the pace of portfolio company exits.
